Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Law n°14-023/AU of 24 June 2014 specifically institutes the carte d'identite comorienne numerique (biometrique) — a dedicated digital/biometric identity card regulation.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The Ministry of Justice Comoros site verifies Décret n°14-137/PR (28 Aug 2024) promulgating Loi n°14-023/AU (24 June 2014), which institutes the biometric/digital national ID card — a dedicated digital ID regulation distinct from the general 1987 ID law. Independently corroborated by the World Bank ID4D Comoros country profile, which cites the same 2014 law. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed on two authoritative sources.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The national identity card is free of charge for first issuance. A fee applies in case of loss or theft (12,300 Comorian francs / approx. 25 EUR noted for French CNIS, similar applies to national ID). First issuance is free.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source is about the French CNI issued by the French Embassy to French nationals resident in Comoros — it does not concern the Comorian national ID system at all, so it cannot support this score. Comoros' own 1987 ID law (Loi n°87-012, Art.6) imposes a "droit de timbre fiscal" on issuance/duplicates of the national ID card, and Comores Infos (12 Jan 2018), quoting the Interior Minister, confirms citizens paid 4,000 rising to 5,000 KMF to obtain the biometric national ID card. No evidence of a free first-issuance policy was found for the Comorian card itself. Value Code changed from 2 (Yes/free) to 1 (No/not free).

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Resident IDs (residency permits and cards) are available to foreign nationals in Comoros according to Smile ID documentation. Foreign nationals residing in Comoros can access some identity documentation but not the national identity card itself.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source (a Smile ID marketing/KYC page) only loosely lists 'Resident IDs' among document types it can verify and does not itself establish eligibility rules. Confirmed instead via Comoros' foreigners' law (Loi n°82-026, amended by Loi n°88-025), which creates a separate carte de séjour/carte de résident regime for foreign residents, while the 1987 ID law (Art.2) reserves the national identity card for Comorian citizens only; UNHCR notes Comoros has no national asylum system, so refugees are documented by UNHCR rather than issued state ID. This supports 'Some' non-national eligibility (residency documentation, not the CNI). Value Code 2 confirmed on stronger primary legal sources.
